text:
sarah.z: Quick sync on Galaxy POC — they asked for the hosted API key lifecycle: creation, recommended rotation cadence, and how we revoke immediately if needed. Kickoff next Monday, want the ops checklist by EOD tomorrow.

matt.s: I can draft a step-by-step. TL;DR: create scoped key with tags, set TTL for short-lived, enable IP allowlist + audit logs, store secret in their vault or our secure notes, and provide an emergency revocation contact.

jin.k: +1 to IP allowlist and audit. For enterprise POCs we require audit-log retention enabled and an initial security questionnaire answer: keys must be rotatable without app redeploy (use short-lived tokens or a secret proxy). Also: recommend 7–14 day TTL for POC keys.

alex.g: Implementation notes for eng teams — hosted keys support both perpetual and expiring tokens. Prefer expiring tokens for POCs. Example create via API: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/keys 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD_ADMIN_TOKEN" 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
 -d '{"name":"galaxy-poc-staging","scopes":["inference:read","embeddings:create"],"tags":{"customer":"galaxy","poc":"galaxy-2026-03"},"expires_in":604800,"allowlist_ips":["203.0.113.45/32"]}'
```
expires_in is in seconds — example above = 7 days. Tagging is critical so we can find/revoke all keys for a POC easily.

matt.s: For rotation: either issue a new key and swap OR use our ephemeral token service. If using swap, create new key, update their config (we provide a one-liner), then revoke old key. Quick swap snippet: 
```bash
# create new key (returns id/new_secret)
# update app env var (example uses jq to patch k8s secret)
kubectl set env deploy/galaxy-app REDWOOD_API_KEY=<new_secret> --namespace=galaxy-staging
# verify requests succeed, then revoke old key
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/keys/<old_key_id>/revoke -H "Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD_ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
Keep rotation in the POC runbook: create -> validate -> revoke old.

jin.k: For revocation semantics — when you call the revoke endpoint we immediately mark key as disabled at the control plane and push a cache-buster to edge nodes. In practice there can be a tiny propagation window (~1–5s) for long-lived connections. Document that to the customer. Also keep an audit event ID for the revoke call.

key-ops-bot: NOTE: keys created with the hosted API must include at least one tag and an owner field. Missing tags will cause onboarding delays.

alex.g: Ops checklist I propose to hand to sales: 
- Create key with tags: customer, poc, env
- Set expires_in (7 days recommended) or use ephemeral tokens
- Enable IP allowlist if customer requires
- Turn on audit logs & retention 90 days (POC default)
- Store secret in vault (hashicorp/1password) and share via secure link
- Add entry to POC runbook with key_id and audit_event template
- Schedule automated reminder to rotate at T-1 day before expiry
- Shared escalation: sales-eng -> solutions -> oncall (eng-oncall) for emergency revokes

matt.s: I'll attach that checklist in the Galaxy onboarding packet and include the curl snippets + k8s swap example. Also flag pricing note: hosted POC keys on free tier limited to 50k tokens/day; if they need higher throughput, we recommend a Dedicated pool trial.

sarah.z: Perfect. Jin, anything else for the security questionnaire answers we need to populate?

jin.k: Add this: "Keys are revocable via control-plane API; revocation is logged with event_id and pushed to edge within seconds. POC keys default to 7 days and are tagged for ownership. IP allowlists supported. For higher assurance, recommend Dedicated or Private deployment."

matt.s: I'll send the updated runbook + revocation playbook by 18:00 PT. tagging @sarah.z for visibility. :thumbsup:

sarah.z: Thanks team — this is exactly what Galaxy asked for. We'll include the one-liners and the escalation contacts in the onboarding email.
